sections.skill: Use simple checklists to start and end work with helpers

questions.prompt: What is onboarding?

choices.text: Setting up a new helper to succeed
Loading boxes onto a delivery truck

questions.correct_answer: Setting up a new helper to succeed
questions.intro: ONBOARDING sets up a new helper to succeed and keeps the business safe: a written role description, any required paperwork, training with the checklists, their own logins with limited access, and who to ask for help. OFFBOARDING happens when someone leaves: remove their access the same day, collect keys and equipment, transfer any files or customer conversations they handled, settle final pay as required, and thank them. Both are easier with a simple checklist.

sections.skill: Moving into and out of an apartment

questions.prompt: Getting keys when moving in is like what?
questions.intro: When you move into an apartment, you get keys, learn where things are, and sign papers. When you move out, you return the keys, take your things, and leave a forwarding address. Starting and ending work with a helper is the same pair of steps: give access and information at the start, then take back access and pass on their work at the end.
